--- a/context.go
+++ b/context.go
@@ -76,6 +76,12 @@ type Context struct {
 
 	// methodNotAllowed hint
 	methodNotAllowed bool
+
+	// methodsAllowed holds the methods registered for the route that matched
+	// the request path when the request method did not. It is filled in only
+	// while routing ends in a 405, in ascending method order, so that the 405
+	// handler can set the Allow header.
+	methodsAllowed []methodTyp
 }
 
 // Reset a routing context to its initial state.
@@ -91,9 +97,26 @@ func (x *Context) Reset() {
 	x.routeParams.Keys = x.routeParams.Keys[:0]
 	x.routeParams.Values = x.routeParams.Values[:0]
 	x.methodNotAllowed = false
+	x.methodsAllowed = x.methodsAllowed[:0]
 	x.parentCtx = nil
 }
 
+// allowMethod adds a method to the allowed methods, keeping them in ascending
+// method order and free of duplicates, so that the Allow header of a 405
+// response is the same on every request however the routing tree was walked.
+func (x *Context) allowMethod(m methodTyp) {
+	i := 0
+	for i < len(x.methodsAllowed) && x.methodsAllowed[i] < m {
+		i++
+	}
+	if i < len(x.methodsAllowed) && x.methodsAllowed[i] == m {
+		return
+	}
+	x.methodsAllowed = append(x.methodsAllowed, 0)
+	copy(x.methodsAllowed[i+1:], x.methodsAllowed[i:])
+	x.methodsAllowed[i] = m
+}
+
 // URLParam returns the corresponding URL parameter value from the request
 // routing context.
 func (x *Context) URLParam(key string) string {
diff --git a/cors.go b/cors.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d4ca0d5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/cors.go
@@ -0,0 +1,347 @@
+package chi
+
+import (
+	"net/http"
+	"sort"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// CORSOptions configures the built-in CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)
+// support of CORS, Mux.EnableCORSWithOptions and Mux.WithCORS.
+type CORSOptions struct {
+	// AllowOrigin is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Use "*" to
+	// allow any origin, or one origin such as "https://example.com". Browsers
+	// refuse "*" for requests that carry credentials, so name an origin when
+	// AllowCredentials is set.
+	AllowOrigin string
+
+	// AllowMethods is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Methods on a preflight
+	// response. When it is empty, the methods that the requested path has a
+	// handler for are used, found in the routing tree.
+	AllowMethods []string
+
+	// AllowHeaders is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Headers on a preflight
+	// response. When it is empty, the headers named by the preflight request
+	// are allowed, or the common headers of DefaultCORSOptions if it names none.
+	AllowHeaders []string
+
+	// ExposeHeaders is the value of Access-Control-Expose-Headers: the response
+	// headers that scripts of other origins may read.
+	ExposeHeaders []string
+
+	// MaxAge is how many seconds a browser may cache a preflight response, sent
+	// as Access-Control-Max-Age. Zero sends no header, so the browser uses its
+	// own default; -1 tells the browser not to cache.
+	MaxAge int
+
+	// AllowCredentials sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true, so that
+	// browsers send cookies and authorization headers with cross-origin
+	// requests.
+	AllowCredentials bool
+}
+
+// DefaultCORSOptions returns the options that EnableCORS uses: any origin, the
+// methods found for each path, the common request headers and a preflight
+// cache of one hour.
+func DefaultCORSOptions() CORSOptions {
+	return CORSOptions{
+		AllowOrigin:  "*",
+		AllowHeaders: append([]string(nil), corsCommonHeaders...),
+		MaxAge:       3600,
+	}
+}
+
+// corsCommonHeaders are the request headers that a preflight response allows
+// by default.
+var corsCommonHeaders = []string{
+	"Accept", "Authorization", "Content-Type", "X-CSRF-Token", "X-Requested-With",
+}
+
+// corsFallbackMethods are named by a preflight response for a path that has no
+// route, where there are no methods to find.
+const corsFallbackMethods = "GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS"
+
+// CORS returns a middleware that sets the CORS headers on every response and
+// answers preflight requests with 204 No Content, without calling the next
+// handler.
+//
+// A preflight request is an OPTIONS request that has an
+// Access-Control-Request-Method header, or one for a path that has no OPTIONS
+// handler of its own. When AllowMethods is empty, the response names the
+// methods that the path has a handler for, found through the routing context
+// of the request, so the middleware is meant to run inside a chi router; it
+// works without one but then names a fixed list of methods.
+func CORS(options CORSOptions) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
+	return newCORSPolicy(options, nil).middleware
+}
+
+// EnableCORS adds CORS support to the router with DefaultCORSOptions. See
+// EnableCORSWithOptions.
+func (mx *Mux) EnableCORS() {
+	mx.EnableCORSWithOptions(DefaultCORSOptions())
+}
+
+// EnableCORSWithOptions adds CORS support to the router: the CORS middleware,
